I've been farming my 4.1 mu for 15 years now, wheat in winter and maize in summer, every year the same. I know this land. This October I will sow wheat on the whole piece. I buy the improved wheat seed from the dealer in town — the kind in the red bag — about 25 jin per mu, so 100 jin total for my plot. Before sowing I run the rotary tiller to chop up the maize stalks. At sowing time I spread one 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer per mu — the 15-15-15 kind — that's 4 bags costing me about 120 yuan each. Then in spring, when the wheat starts jointing, I top-dress with urea, about 30 jin per mu. I learned that from my neighbor Lao Wang: he skipped top-dressing two years ago and his yield dropped by nearly 100 jin per mu. I irrigate three times — after sowing to get it up, at jointing in March, and once at heading. The electricity for the well pump is expensive but I can't skip it. For pesticides, I spray herbicide once after sowing, and if I see aphids in spring I spray insecticide once more. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather is normal.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in early June. I always use hybrid seed — comes in small packets, about 3 jin per mu, 12 jin total. I don't till for maize, just direct seed into the wheat stubble with the no-till planter — saves diesel and three days of work, which matters because the rain could come. At sowing I put down compound fertilizer, about 40 kg per mu, and when the maize is knee-high I spread urea, about 20 kg per mu. I irrigate twice if it's dry — at the trumpet stage and when the tassels come out. Two pesticide sprays: herbicide once, then one for corn borer. I expect about 520 kg per mu.

Fertilizer prices went up again this year, and my wife says we should cut back because our daughter needs school fees. But I won't reduce my fertilizer — I tried saving 50 yuan per mu on fertilizer five years ago and lost almost 80 kg per mu. A bad harvest is a disaster; wasting a bit of fertilizer is just a cost. I watch what Lao Wang does with his 6 mu next to mine, and we mostly do the same thing. If it works, I don't change it.
